Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed a sustained 429 spike starting 2026-03-29T00:38:06Z from request IDs matching the nimbus fleet. Correlated with increased retry volume from their IP range.
- Root cause (preliminary): during the deployment yesterday that migrated several org namespaces we incorrectly mapped Nimbus Health's primary project to the 'dev-tier' quota set instead of the 'enterprise-tier'. The tiering table (org_project_tiers) had a stale alias (nimbus --> nimbus-legacy) and our automated re-tiering job resolved the alias to the wrong policy.
- Consequence: rate limit counters (per-project and per-org) applied lower burst/throttle thresholds, producing 429s; client retries then re-submitted requests leading to temporary 5xx errors downstream as workers saturated.

Immediate mitigation proposed (we can execute in ~15–30m):
1) Apply a temporary override to assign nimbus-prod-us-east-1 to enterprise-tier (manual write to routing_policy). This will raise per-second quotas and burst windows.
2) Pause the automated re-tiering job to avoid flip-flop.
3) Add strict retry-after headers in the gateway for 429s to reduce retry storms (config change).
4) Add a short-term token-level circuit breaker for very high retry rates on that project.

I'll attach a filtered log bundle and a dif of the tiering table so legal/ops can see the change. After we stabilize we'll run a scoped config fix and a postmortem.
